newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks close sharply off, break support.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks close sharply off, break support.

text.p: Mexican stocks broke support and closed down for the seventh session in a row on Monday on lack of investor interest, traders and analysts said.
"We broke an important support at 3,250 points, after which dealers continued to sell a little," said Roberto Solano, deputy research director at the Estrategia Bursatil brokerage.
"We see a stronger support at 3,200 points, where there may be some opportunities to buy," he added.
The blue chip IPC index closed down 41.64 points, or 1.27 percent, at 3,246.65. Volume was lackluster at 56.4 million shares traded.
Dealers said that market apathy was due to caution over the political and social situation in Mexico and international investors preferring a bullish Dow Jones.

"Political and social concerns are overriding the economic situation which, without exaggerating, is satisfactory. I think uncertainty has increased due to the prospect of confrontation prior to the (mid-term congressional) elections in 1997," Solano added.
The Dow Jones ended up 76.03 points, or 1.12 percent, at another record close of 6,547.79.
On the broad market, 103 stocks changed hands, of which losers well outnumbered gainers by 61 to 19.
Financial stock GFInver headed the gainers' list, up four centavos at 68. Traders noted the stock had been favorably priced as GFInver will be taken over by Spanish bank Santander.
Debt-ridden holding company Sidek headed the losers, down 15 centavos to 1.00 peso.
